in_text_mentions: any clinical or mycological evidence of a fungal infection. There was no history of fever, joint pain, or myalgia. The systems review was unremarkable, with no significant medical or family history. Cutaneous examination showed non-scaly, erythematous to violaceous lesions that were mostly distributed over the flexural and intertriginous areas, such as the genital, thigh, axilla, inframammary, antecubital fossae, and neck regions (Figures 1, 2). Other areas beyond the flexural regions were also involved, indicating a more generalized distribution. Hair, nails, and mucous membranes were normal.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient showing symmetric, well-demarcated erythematous plaques involving both buttocks in a butterfly/V-shaped distribution across the gluteal cleft. The caption and in-text explicitly link this eruption to amoxicillin drug provocation in a patient with SDRIFE (article title), and the gluteal/intertriginous involvement with bilateral symmetry matches the disease's classic presentation. No other disease is mentioned for this panel and no third-party copyright is indicated.
panels.attribution_text: Letón-Cabanillas et al. Symmetrical Drug-Related Intertriginous and Flexural Exanthema With Amoxicillin: Presenting a Flare-Up Phenomenon.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.74393. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Bilateral gluteal erythematous plaques following positive amoxicillin drug provocation test
in_text_mentions: d amoxicillin extract (20 mg/mL) (Lab Diater®, Madrid, Spain), was performed with negative readings at 15 minutes and 24 hours. Therefore, a DPT with amoxicillin was initiated following our protocol for delayed reactions. On the first day, half of the minimum effective dose (250 mg) was administered. The following day, the full dose (500 mg) was given. Subsequently, the patient continued with home treatment at a dosage of 500 mg every 12 hours. After three days of home treatment, the patient experienced bilateral pruritic and erythematous plaques in the gluteal and inguinal regions (Figure 1).

Black bars/ovals are anonymization overlays.

in_text_mentions: A 53-year-old obese female presented to the dermatology outpatient department of a tertiary care centre with complaints of a burning, erythematous rash predominantly affecting the flexural regions for the past seven to 12 days. The eruption initially appeared over the perineum and gluteal cleft, later spreading to involve the groin, inframammary folds, axillae, and the area beneath the abdominal pannus (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: well-defined, symmetrical erythema involving the axillae

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph from an SDRIFE-focused case report showing well-demarcated flexural erythema with desquamation; caption and title support SDRIFE attribution. B: Clinical photograph panel showing well-demarcated symmetrical erythema of the lower abdomen with superficial desquamation, consistent with the captioned SDRIFE eruption. C: Clinical photograph of the groin/inguinal folds showing symmetrical well-demarcated erythema with superficial desquamation, supporting SDRIFE per caption and article focus.
panels.attribution_text: Singh et al. Symmetrical Drug-Related Intertriginous and Flexural Exanthema (SDRIFE) Unfolded: Diagnostic Pitfalls and Psoriatic Confounders Among Flexural Dermatoses.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.93524. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Presence of well-defined, symmetrical erythema accompanied by superficial desquamation involving the groin, axillae, inframammary areas, and lower abdomen.
in_text_mentions: In her previous flares, inverse psoriasis had typically manifested as well-demarcated erythematous patches within axillae, groin, and inframammary folds, without appreciable scaling owing to constant flexural moisture. In contrast, the current eruption showed well-defined, symmetrical erythema accompanied by superficial desquamation involving the groin, axillae, inframammary areas, and lower abdomen (Figure 2).
